subject: VPC pin offboarding + hotpatch ladder — coordination and rollback plan
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: VPC pin offboarding + hotpatch ladder — coordination and rollback plan

Hi Sanjay,

Following our recent security audit, we need to apply a critical CVE hotpatch to the private VPC fleet and then perform a controlled offboarding of the legacy pinned runtime (v2.8.1) so we can stage the lighter v3.0.0 runtime for production canaries. High-level proposal:

- Stage 1 (hotpatch): install minimal security-only patches on pinned nodes; no version switch.
- Stage 2 (pin-offboarding): unpin a small subset (2 nodes per AZ), upgrade those to v3.0.0-lite and route ~2% traffic.
- Stage 3 (ramp or revert): if canaries pass steady-state health for 30m, ramp to 20%; if not, automatically revert to v2.8.1.

Operational asks from your side:
1) Confirm a 2-hour maintenance window on Tue 2026-09-21 — proposed 02:00–04:00 UTC.
2) Tell us whether any IP allowlist or firewall egress changes are required for the canary.
3) Provide a DR contact for your network ops and confirm certificate owners for TLS rotation (if we need to rotate).

We attached a short decision matrix and our smoke test checklist: pin-offboard-matrix.xlsx, hotpatch-smoke-tests.txt.

If that window doesn't work, propose an alternate 2-hour period this week and we'll adjust the canary plan accordingly. Once we have sign-off we'll lock the runbook and schedule a 30-minute walk-through with your infra and our oncall.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

attachments: pin-offboard-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), hotpatch-smoke-tests.txt (text)

Subject: Re: VPC pin offboarding + hotpatch ladder — coordination and rollback plan

Grace —

Thanks for the clear plan. A couple of notes from Acme infra:
- The proposed 02:00–04:00 UTC window is acceptable on our side if we limit the canary to 1–2 nodes per AZ.
- We will need a 30-minute heads-up before any firewall rule changes; our firewall team will only allow temporary egress to the new control-plane IPs for the duration of the canary (they want the timestamped change request).
- For TLS rotation: certs are owned by Priya (cc'd). Priya, can you confirm whether a new cert will be required or whether the existing certs are valid through 2027?

Please include the exact IP ranges and ASN that the canary nodes will call out to; our SOC needs that for the change ticket.

On the rollback: we need explicit timeboxes (e.g., stop ramp at 30m if error-rate > 1% or p95 increases by > 40%). Those thresholds will trigger our network rollback and a remediation bridge.

Sanjay
Head of Infrastructure, AcmeHealth

Hi all,

Thanks — a few engineering details and the concrete rollback runbook attached. I've included the main gating rules below so everyone has the exact operational criteria:

Planned sequence (detailed):
1) Preflight (T-24h): run automated canary smoke on staging using the same network ACLs + certs; confirm KV cache sanity and disk pressure < 65%.
2) Hotpatch (T+0): patch kernel + runtime CVE fix on pinned nodes (no version switch). Quick smoke: start 5 synthetic prompts, confirm latency p95 within baseline +15%.
3) Offboard canary (T+15m): unpin 2 nodes per AZ, deploy v3.0.0-lite; route 2% of traffic via split proxy.
4) Canary watch (T+45m): health windows — error-rate < 1%, p95 <= baseline*1.4, tail latency no more than +200ms. If thresholds breached, immediate automated revert to v2.8.1 for those nodes.

Rollback specifics (also in rollback-runbook.pdf):
- Automated revert: we maintain a snapshot of the pinned node image; revert script is idempotent and has a gate that prevents cascading unpin across AZs.
- KV-drain: before unpin we trim active sessions, copy KV snapshots to temporary keyed store for fast restore (estimated 60s per node).
- Network safety: we will perform BGP dampening checks before the canary and disable graceful restart across the canary nodes to avoid route churn.
- Post-change telemetry: we push detailed traces (sampling 100%) to the canary trace bucket for 30m and tag spans with "acme-canary-20260921".

Operational asks (action items):
- Sanjay: confirm IP ranges (we will provide control-plane IPs in the runbook) and the 30-minute firewall SLAs.
- Laura: please approve the canary authorization and the security signoff.
- Neha: please confirm logging/retention tweaks below.

Attachments: rollback-runbook.pdf (detailed procedures + commands and playbook).

–Karthik
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Karthik / Grace / Sanjay —

Approve the plan with the following conditions:
- Final window: Tue 2026-09-21 02:00–04:00 UTC (Redwood to kick at 02:00 UTC sharp).
- Canary: strictly 2 nodes per AZ, 2% traffic cap. No ramp without explicit oncall + Acme network ops ACK.
- Timeboxes: if any threshold breaches within the first 30 minutes we must revert immediately; if we pass 30m without regressions we can proceed to 20% ramp after a coordinated bridge check-in.
- Compliance evidence: provide post-run audit logs for the maintenance window (syscalls + network ACL diffs) and a signed maintenance exception document.

Neha, please confirm whether the log retention change to 90 days for the canary trace bucket is sufficient for compliance.

Sanjay — once you confirm firewall window mechanics I will sign off formally and instruct the oncall to standby for the bridge.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Production Operations
